title: Introduce typed-annotation backfill and rollback briefs
author: Priya Khatri
description:
Context: onboarding submissions have proliferated freeform attributes (free-form strings, vendor-specific keys, and shallow typing) which harms deterministic compatibility checks and automated release note generation. This PR introduces a conservative typed-annotation backfill pipeline and a compact rollback-brief generator so that (1) profiles gain explicit typed attributes for downstream comparators, and (2) every automated release brief includes a machine-readable rollback hint.

What this PR does (single-string summary): adds a backfill worker that derives typed annotations for existing model profiles based on a small rule set + sampled telemetry, a migration to stamp 'typed_schema_v1' where confidence >= 0.85, a compact JSONL release-brief serializer for change automation, and a roll-forward/rollback brief generator that supplies actionable rollback keys for downstream release tooling.

Implementation notes: the backfill worker lives in registry/ingest/typed_backfill.py; it runs as a job that samples 5k profiles per cohort, computes candidate typed attributes (enum detection, numeric ranges, tokenization hints) and emits a confidence score per attribute. Typing decisions are stored as top-level attributes under 'typed_annotations' with a schema_version and provenance hash. We only stamp profiles when the overall profile confidence crosses the configured threshold (default 0.85) to avoid noisy writes. The release brief serializer is a compact JSONL writer (registry/release/compact_brief.py) designed for fast indexing by the release assembler.

Migration strategy and rollout: this was deployed behind a feature flag (model-typed-backfill). Backfill runs in opt-in mode for first 48 hours (dry-run + metrics) and then a controlled write-pass was executed for 35% of profile traffic cohorts, observed in canary dashboards for stability and index sizes. Rollback briefs are emitted whenever a profile stamp is reverted by the backfill operator or an automated rollback rule triggers (e.g. provenance mismatch).

Testing and validation: unit tests for rule heuristics + property-based tests for enum detection added (tests/ingest/test_typed_backfill.py). Integration test that runs the backfill against a sampled fixture of 200 synthetic profiles and validates that release briefs include rollback_hints and provenance stamps. Load test confirms the worker sustains expected throughput (~120 profiles/sec) without affecting ingest cluster CPU beyond 5%.

Why conservative typing: previous attempts to aggressively infer types caused false positive release churn (see earlier gdocs linked in ENG-1014). This design favors under-annotation and explicit confidence thresholds to limit release noise.

Follow-ups (future PRs): 1) automated feedback loop to surface false-positives to curation UI (ENG-1721); 2) migration summarizer for historical release brief backfilling across longer retention windows.

ci_checks: load-test: pass (local synthetic load within target)
release_notes: Adds a conservative typed-annotation backfill for model profiles (typed_schema_v1 stamps), a compact release-brief serializer, and rollback-brief hints to support safer automated rollouts. Migration gated by feature flag and confidence threshold. Operators: review docs/model-registry/typed-annotations.md for configuration and rollback guidance.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: model-typed-backfill. Default confidence threshold: 0.85. Backfill job schedules: hourly, sample size 5k. To revert stamps run migrations/20250923_stamp_typed_schema.py --revert with dry-run=false and follow ops guide in docs/model-registry/typed-annotations.md.
changelog_impact: low (non-breaking): writes additional typed_annotations metadata and introduces compact briefs for release automation. Consumers should ignore typed_annotations if not ready; validator returns a soft-warning by default.
qa_summary: QA ran integration fixture, property tests for heuristics, and a 48-hour dry-run canary on 35% cohorts. No functional regressions observed; minor index size growth (+2.1% per cohort) within acceptable limits.
additional_context: Operator safety was prioritized: provenance hashes, TTL and dry-run gating ensure we can surgically revert stamps when needed. This PR is deliberately conservative to reduce churn in release automation and allow downstream consumers to opt-in to typed metadata.
